method: Primary verification by the author against named sources. Gemini used once as a second reader, flagging only.

claims.text: The Moon is receding from Earth at about 3.8 cm per year.
claims.as_written: drifting away from us at about three point eight centimetres a year
claims.source: NASA Lunar Laser Ranging / NASA Lunar Fact Sheet

claims.text: The Moon's mean distance from Earth is about 384,400 km.
claims.as_written: about three hundred and eighty four thousand kilometres away
claims.source: NASA Lunar Fact Sheet (semi-major axis 384,400 km)

claims.text: The Moon's mass is 7.35e22 kg, i.e. 7.35e19 tonnes = 73 billion billion tonnes (short scale).
claims.as_written: It weighs about seventy three billion billion tonnes
claims.source: NASA Lunar Fact Sheet (mass 7.346e22 kg)

claims.text: Tidal force scales as the inverse cube of distance, so halving the distance multiplies it by eight.
claims.as_written: Tidal force scales with the inverse cube of distance ... Cut the distance in half, and the pull that stretches our planet becomes eight times stronger
claims.source: Standard tidal theory: differential gravity across a body goes as 2GMr/d^3

claims.text: The Earth-Moon Roche limit is ~9,500 km (rigid) to ~18,400 km (fluid) from Earth's centre.
claims.as_written: somewhere between about nine and a half and eighteen thousand kilometres from Earth's centre
claims.source: Roche limit d = 1.26R(rho_E/rho_m)^(1/3) rigid, 2.44R fluid; Earth R=6371 km, densities 5514 and 3344 kg/m3

claims.text: The solid Earth body tide has a vertical amplitude of roughly 30-40 cm for the main lunar (M2) component.
claims.as_written: rises and falls by roughly thirty to forty centimetres twice a day
claims.source: Earth tide constituent table: M2 vertical amplitude 384.83 mm

claims.text: Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System, driven by tidal heating from Jupiter.
claims.as_written: Jupiter's moon Io is squeezed by exactly this kind of tidal kneading, and it is the most volcanically active object in the solar system
claims.source: NASA Galileo and Juno mission science; NASA Io overview

claims.text: Oceans cover about 71% of Earth's surface.
claims.as_written: Seventy percent of this planet's surface is ocean
claims.source: NOAA: about 71 percent of the Earth's surface is water-covered

claims.text: Roughly 38-40% of the world's population lives within 100 km of a coast.
claims.as_written: about forty percent of humanity lives within a hundred kilometres of a coastline. That is roughly three billion people
claims.source: UN environmental indicator methodology sheet (~40%); Small & Nicholls (2003) ~38%

claims.text: Geostationary orbit is 35,786 km above the surface, i.e. 42,164 km from Earth's centre.
claims.as_written: Geostationary satellites ... sit about thirty five thousand eight hundred kilometres up
claims.source: Standard orbital mechanics; ESA/NASA orbit definitions

claims.text: GPS satellites orbit at about 20,200 km altitude.
claims.as_written: the navigation constellations at around twenty thousand kilometres
claims.source: US Space Force / GPS.gov: ~20,200 km MEO

claims.text: Saturn's main rings span roughly 280,000 km and are as little as ~10 m thick in places.
claims.as_written: they are over two hundred and eighty thousand kilometres across, and in places they are only about ten metres thick
claims.source: NASA Cassini mission ring science

claims.text: Earth's axial tilt is about 23.4 degrees.
claims.as_written: about twenty three and a half degrees
claims.source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet (obliquity 23.44 deg)

claims.text: Whether the Moon is REQUIRED to stabilise Earth's obliquity is contested. Laskar et al. (1993) found a moonless Earth could vary chaotically up to ~85 deg; Lissauer, Barnes & Chambers (2012) found variation typically confined to a ~20-25 deg range.
claims.as_written: presented as a genuine scientific disagreement rather than as settled fact
claims.source: Laskar, Joutel & Robutel, Nature 361 (1993); Lissauer, Barnes & Chambers, Icarus 217 (2012)

claims.text: Mars's obliquity varies far more widely than Earth's over millions of years.
claims.as_written: Mars, which has only two tiny moons, is thought to have wandered over a much wider range of tilt across its history
claims.source: Laskar & Robutel (1993); NASA Mars climate history

claims.text: Earth's day is lengthening by roughly 1.7-2.3 ms per century from tidal friction.
claims.as_written: lengthening by roughly two milliseconds per century
claims.source: Stephenson & Morrison, eclipse records; IERS

claims.text: Fossil growth bands indicate a day of roughly 21-22 hours several hundred million years ago.
claims.as_written: a day several hundred million years ago was around twenty two hours long
claims.source: Palaeontological rhythmite and coral banding studies (Wells 1963 and successors)

claims.text: Light takes about 0.04-0.06 s to travel 11,600-18,000 km.
claims.as_written: Light takes a few hundredths of a second to reach you from that distance

claims.text: Deep-sea hydrothermal vent ecosystems are chemosynthetic and do not depend on sunlight.
claims.as_written: Deep ocean ecosystems around hydrothermal vents do not care about sunlight at all
claims.source: NOAA Ocean Exploration: chemosynthesis at hydrothermal vents

claims.text: Lunar mare volcanism largely ceased between about 3 and 2 billion years ago.
claims.as_written: a world whose great volcanic era ended two to three billion years ago
claims.source: Apollo sample dating; NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter results
